messages:
emma: quick question — running into weird behavior when our JS SDK auto-refreshes auth mid-stream. Using AbortController to cancel, but after token rotate the stream keeps sending until idle timeout. Anyone run into this?

sanjay: which sdk + version + repro steps?

emma: js sdk v2.3.1. pattern: start stream with AbortController.signal, leave it open ~55m, server triggers 401+refresh, client retries, then when we call controller.abort() the stream doesn't terminate immediately. logs show 401 then 200 on the retry.

oliver: likely the retry path isn't carrying the original AbortSignal. retries create a fresh request and we forget to wire the signal through. that would allow the retried request to ignore abort.

mxiao: yup — python has a similar gap: we map context/timeout to a cancel token, but if the auth refresh happens in a background thread the cancel can race and not affect the new request.

natalie: curious — does this create any risk of leaking partial content across users or tokens?

emma: we didn't see user data crossing, just duplicate partial chunks during the retry. still bad UX and could increase billing.

sanjay: short term: add an opt-out that disables auto token refresh for streaming requests (config flag). long term: propagate abort/context through retry logic.

oliver: i'll open a PR to ensure the fetch wrapper attaches the AbortSignal to all retry attempts. test should simulate mid-stream 401->200 and call abort after retry starts.

mxiao: i'll do the python side — add cancel_token param to stream call and ensure any retry spawns inherit that token. will add unit tests for thread-based refresh race.

emma: example usage from repro: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rhd-3', messages, signal: ac.signal });
// later
ac.abort();
```
Would be great if that reliably tears down even if auth rotates mid-request.

oliver: plan: patch js fetch wrapper + tests, patch python mapping, add go check (context.Context must be threaded through retries), add e2e.

sdk-bot: ISSUE-4123 created: "streaming: preserve abort signal across auth-refresh retries" — assigned to @oliver and @mxiao

qa-ops: i'll add an e2e that rotates service token during an active stream and asserts immediate close on abort.

natalie: reminder for dedicated/private docs — update changelog and ops notes; long-lived streams common for enterprise.

oliver: will coordinate release plan: patch -> canary minor release with opt-in flag -> monitor -> full roll.

emma: thanks all — ping me if you want me to add a small repro in the demos repo.
